terms.title: Terms of use
terms.body: FantasyWiki is a non-commercial university project, provided as-is and without any warranty. Playing is free and the in-game budget and points have no monetary value.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: You sign in with your Google account. We store only your name, email address and profile picture, kept in a session cookie and alongside your game data (teams and leagues). There are no ads, analytics or other tracking.

attribution.title: Wikimedia attribution
attribution.body: Pageview data comes from the Wikimedia Pageviews API. Article titles and content belong to Wikipedia and are available under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license. FantasyWiki is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Wikimedia Foundation.

start.title: Welcome to FantasyWiki
start.lede: Fantasy sport played with Wikipedia. You sign contracts on real articles, and they score for you on the days people actually read them.
start.credits: to spend in your first league
start.win: at the end of the league wins
start.formHint: Next stop is your dashboard, with the tour running beside it.

teamRequired.title: Create your team to start playing
teamRequired.body: You are signed in but have not named a team yet. Create one to join the Global League and start playing.

stats.title: Points and credits
stats.body: Yesterday's points, what is left of your credits, and how you stand. This ledger is your team in one glance.

league.title: Your league
league.body: You start in the Global League. Each league keeps its own budget, market and standings, and you switch between them here.

market.title: The market
market.body: Every article shows what people are reading and what a contract costs. Sign one and it scores for you from the next daily update.

formation.title: The pitch
formation.body: Place your articles on the pitch. Two that link to each other on Wikipedia pay a bonus when their spots are connected.

wrap.title: That is the tour
wrap.body: Sign your first contracts whenever you are ready. You can replay this from the menu any time.

manageTeam.title: Getting to your pitch
manageTeam.body: Your formation lives one click away, behind this button. There is no menu entry for it, so this is the way in.

guide.title: How FantasyWiki works
guide.lede: What decides your score, what decides your prices, and what you can do about either.

day.title: A day in the league
day.body: Every morning your articles are scored on how many people read them the day before. Those daily scores stack up for the whole league, and the highest total wins it.

contrast.title: Points follow today, prices follow the month
contrast.body: You score on yesterday's readers. A contract costs what the last 30 days of readers say it is worth. The same article can be loud on one side and quiet on the other.

spike.title: Quiet page, big day
spike.alt: Thirty flat days ending in one huge spike
spike.note: Cheap to sign, because its price still reads a quiet month. It pays once, then goes quiet again.

steady.title: Read every day
steady.alt: Thirty days of consistently high readership
steady.note: Priced for what it is, and it pays again tomorrow.

contrast.takeaway: Catching a rise early is the cheap way to score. Holding a favourite is the dependable one. Most teams want some of each.

points.title: What a reader is worth
points.alt: Readers in a day plotted against the points they earn
points.rule: Every doubling of readers adds a point, starting at one point for 4,000 readers a day. Past 150,000 readers, each extra 50,000 adds another point.
points.floor: Under 2,000 readers a day an article scores nothing. Those articles also cost nothing to sign, which is how a team with no credits gets back on its feet.

chemistry.title: Chemistry between your picks
chemistry.alt: Three connected spots showing what each kind of Wikipedia link pays
chemistry.mutual: They link to each other on Wikipedia
chemistry.oneway: One of them links to the other
chemistry.body: Chemistry is only counted between spots your formation connects, so where you place an article matters as much as which one you signed.
chemistry.cap: A whole formation banks at most {cap} chemistry points, so even a perfectly linked team has a ceiling on the bonus.

contracts.title: Signing, selling, renewing
contracts.hold: You get your credits back, plus or minus however the price moved while you held it.
contracts.sell: You are paid for the days you did not use, at today's price. The days you did use are spent.
contracts.renew: On the last day you choose. Doing nothing lets it go. Renewing the same article again costs 10% more each time you do it in a row.
contracts.budget: You start each league with {credits} credits and room for 11 articles.
contracts.free: Articles nobody is reading are free to sign, so running out of credits is never the end of your league.
